newsitem.title: FINLAND: MERITA UPS FINNISH 97 GDP GROWTH FCAST TO 4.5 PCT.
newsitem.headline: MERITA UPS FINNISH 97 GDP GROWTH FCAST TO 4.5 PCT.

text.p: Finnish banking group Merita Oy said in a statement on Thursday its economic research department had raised its forecast for Finnish Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth in 1997 to 4.5 percent from 4.0 percent.
It forecast growth in 1998 at 3.5 percent.
"Already at the end of last year, growth accelerated stronger than expected and this year's demand outlook has improved slightly across the board," Merita said.
"Home construction investment rose (in 1996) by over a fifth and indicators suggest even bigger investment," it said.
"Exports also rose surprisingly strongly considering that neither the European demand outlook nor the paper industry prices show a proper upturn."
Merita said there were even chances for stonger growth though it was likely that it would slow towards the end of the year, and added it saw no reasons for changed monetary policy.
"Although economic activity is becoming slightlty livelier this year than we earlier estimated, we see no reason to change the tuning of monetary policy this year," the bank said.
"Next year, too, inflation pressures will be small, but at
that time the tuning of monetary policy should naturally already
take into account the situation in 1999," the economists said.
Key figures in Merita's new forecast:
Exports +8 +6 +3.8
Imports (goods) +9 +6 +4.5
Consumption, private +3.5 +3 +3.3
Investment +11 +8 +5.5
Industrial production +6 +5 +3.3
Unemployment 14.5 13.5 15.7
C/A (FIM billion) +16 +21 +20.0
